To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of empirical models based on water constituents to estimate chlorophill-a using multispectral remote sensing is promising in tropical estuarine systems.

the performance of empirical algorithms to estimate chlorophyl-a in turbid tropical estuaries was improved using multispectral data and the two-band algorithm using bands of Sentinel-2/OLI and Sentinel-2/SLC sensors showed a strong potential for future applications.
The application of empirical models based on multispectral remote sensing data to estimate chloropyll-a in productive tropical estuarie-lagoon systems was assessed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of empirical algorithms to estimate chlorophyl-a concentration in a productive tropical coastal system.

the development of new algorithms for estimating chlorophyl-a using multispectral satellite imagery, with the potential to contribute to the improvement of water quality monitoring in productive tropical estuarines.
the development of a robust and reliable approach for the retrieval of chlorophyll concentration using multispectral data in a productive tropical system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NIR-Red three band algorithms are the most appropriate to estimate chlorophyl-a in the study area.
the use of empirical algorithms for estimating chlorophyl-a is promising for turbid and productive tropical estuaria.
the use of multispectral sensors to estimate chlorophyl-a in turbid productive tropical estuires is feasible and promising.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the empirical algorithms based on multispectral reflectance are able to provide accurate estimates of chlorophyll-α in productive tropical estuarines.
the application of NIR-Red models is a reliable option to estimate chlorophyl-a in turbid tropical estuaries.

the use of multispectral data is a promising alternative to estimate chlorophill-a in turbid tropical estuaries, and the application of algorithms based on bands of modern satellite sensors is a promising approach for coming decades.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of chlorophyll algorithms based on multispectral remote sensing data is strongly influenced by the spectral properties of the estuary under study.

standard NIR-Red algorithms can be used to estimate chlorophyl-a in productive tropical estuarines, and that recently launched satellite sensors such as Sentinel-3/OC can be used to monitor the dynamics of chlorophyll in these environments.

empirical models using the NIR-Red band combination can be applied for chlorophyll-a retrieval in tropical estuaries, and also that the use of satellite sensors with bands located in NIR-Red region can provide accurate estimations of chlorophyll in productive tropical estuarines.
